title: Foundation: membership, transitive closure, and rank

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 10, 18, and 30–31 (§2, Foundation; §4, transitive sets; §6, Lemma 6.4, Theorems 6.5–6.6, Definition 6.7, and Exercise 6.8)

based_on.title: Set Theory: An Open Introduction
based_on.pages: 154–159 (§§11.4–11.6, Foundation and ranks; online revision July 2026)

summary: Foundation supports membership induction and an ordinal rank that decreases when passing to a member.
abstract: A set may contain other sets, which in turn have members of their own. The axiom of foundation prevents this membership structure from looping or descending forever, and allows each set to receive an ordinal height called its rank. Passing from a set to one of its members always lowers that height. Rank therefore measures the depth of membership rather than the number of elements: even a set with just one member can have an arbitrarily large rank.
